title: Ethical business behaviour
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:14Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches businesses behaving ethically beyond legal requirements: one covers consumers' ethical purchasing decisions at a Year 9 depth, and the other covers legal duties businesses owe consumers, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Ethical business behaviour
card: Ethics are ideas about what is right and wrong. An ethical business tries to do what is right, not only what the law says it must do.
Treating workers fairly, such as paying them properly and keeping their workplace safe.
Telling the truth about the business and its products, even when a lie might win a sale.
Caring for the environment, such as cutting waste and using less energy.
draft.remember: Ethical businesses aim to do what is right, not just what the law requires, and this can win trust.

a.q: Which best describes an ethical business?
opts: It tries to do what is right, beyond what the law requires
It does only what the law forces it to do
It sets the lowest prices it can in its market
It gives away most of its products for free
a.why: Ethics are about right and wrong, so an ethical business aims to do what is right even where no law makes it. Doing only what the law requires is the minimum, not the whole of ethical behaviour.
a.clue: Think about going further than the rules.

b.q: Sam's Bikes in Geelong could throw away its old packaging, but it chooses to reuse it and cut waste, although no law forces it to. Which type of ethical behaviour is this?
b.why: Reusing packaging and cutting waste is a way of caring for the environment. It is not about workers or honesty, which are different types of ethical behaviour.
b.clue: What is being done with the packaging?

a.best: It tries to do what is right, beyond what the law requires
